Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayva usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, delight and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ayva holds significant cultural relevance in Hinduism. In Hindu mythology, Ayu is the goddess of life and longevity. The name reflects the belief in the value and joy of life. In India, it is a popular name for both girls and boys.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ayva lies in its connection to the Hindu goddess of life and longevity. The name is believed to bring blessings of good health, long life, and prosperity. It is a reminder of the importance of cherishing life and living it to the fullest. The name also holds the energy of the divine feminine, symbolizing nurturing, creativity, and the cycle of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayva is a Sanskrit name meaning "Divine Mother's Grace." It symbolizes the blessings and protection bestowed upon an individual by the divine feminine energy, embodied in the form of the mother goddess.

historical_references.reference: Ayva was an important Jain Tirthankara of the 21st Tirthankara cycle. The 24 Tirthankaras of this cycle were born in Ayodhya, which was ruled by King Trivikrama.
Ayva is also mentioned in Hindu mythology as the wife of sage Vishwamitra. Vishwamitra was a great sage and a powerful magician. Ayva was his second wife, who bore him a son named Shakuni.
